description: 7-principle framework for writing effective goal prompts for autonomous coding agents — exit criteria, direction, measurability, environment, visual targets, progress tracking, and cleanup.

evals.task: The user says: 'Write a goal for an AI agent to improve the performance of our React dashboard. It's slow and our users are complaining.' No metrics, no baseline, no constraints given. The agent applying goal-dl should push back: ask for measurable targets, a starting point, and known constraints before writing any goal.

must_have: ask for a specific measurable target or number
ask for a starting point or current baseline
push back on vagueness before crafting the goal
must_not_have: accept the vague request without asking clarifying questions
write a goal with no specific exit condition

evals.task: The user says: 'I need a goal for a multi-day refactoring agent. It needs to migrate 40 microservices from Express to Fastify, one by one. I'll have the agent running in the background.' The agent applying goal-dl should embed progress tracking (commit milestones, status artifacts) and a cleanup step (review pass, dead-end removal) into the goal prompt.

must_have: suggest commit milestones or draft PR pattern
suggest a living artifact for status visibility
include a review or cleanup step at the end
must_not_have: write a goal with no progress visibility mechanism
omit the cleanup/review step for a days-long run

evals.task: The user says: 'Write a goal for an agent to clone the Stripe landing page. I want pixel-perfect fidelity.' The agent applying goal-dl should warn against pure visual targets, suggest pairing screenshots with functional checklists and design tokens, and ensure the environment is production-like (same framework, same build tools).

must_have: warn about risks of pure visual/pixel-perfect targets
suggest pairing visual references with functional specs or checklists
address the environment (same framework, flags, tools)
must_not_have: write a goal that ignores functional verification
